definitions.explanation: a stick or rod used by a wizard, witch, or fairy to cast spells, common in fairy tales, fantasy stories, and figurative expressions

examples.japanese: {魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}を{振|ふ}った。
{魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}があったらいいのに。
examples.english: I wish I had a magic wand.

examples.japanese: {政治|せいじ}に{魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}はない。{地道|じみち}な{努力|どりょく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: There's no magic wand in politics. Steady effort is what's needed.

notes:
Combines {魔法|まほう} (magic) with の (possessive particle) and {杖|つえ} (cane, staff, stick). Used both literally in fairy tales and fantasy contexts and figuratively to mean a miraculous solution that solves problems instantly. The figurative use often appears in the negative: {魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}はない (there is no magic wand).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}を{振|ふ}る: to wave a magic wand
- {魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}はない: there is no magic wand (figurative)
- {魔法|まほう}の{杖|つえ}を{手|て}に{入|い}れる: to get hold of a magic wand

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {杖|つえ}: cane; walking stick; staff — the general word for a stick used for support or as a tool
- {魔法|まほう}: magic; sorcery — the broader concept of magic
- {打|う}ち{出|で}の{小槌|こづち}: magic mallet — a treasure from Japanese folklore that grants wishes when struck
